name: Numerical Methods
description: Computing with real numbers on real machines: error, root finding, linear systems, interpolation, integration and ODEs.

nodes.name: Floating point
nodes.desc: How IEEE 754 numbers are stored, machine epsilon and rounding.
nodes.summary: You will understand how IEEE 754 floating-point numbers are stored and how rounding and machine epsilon limit numerical accuracy.

nodes.name: Error analysis
nodes.desc: Truncation versus rounding error, error propagation and cancellation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to separate truncation from rounding error, track how errors propagate and avoid catastrophic cancellation.

nodes.name: Conditioning
nodes.desc: Condition numbers and the difference between a hard problem and an unstable algorithm.
nodes.summary: You will be able to measure a problem's sensitivity with condition numbers and tell an ill-conditioned problem from an unstable algorithm.

nodes.name: Root finding
nodes.desc: Bisection, Newton's method, the secant method and convergence rates.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find roots of nonlinear equations with bisection, Newton and secant methods and compare their convergence rates.

nodes.name: Direct solvers
nodes.desc: LU factorisation with pivoting and Cholesky for linear systems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to solve linear systems with LU factorisation with partial pivoting and with Cholesky for symmetric positive definite matrices.

nodes.name: Iterative solvers
nodes.desc: Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel and conjugate gradient methods.
nodes.summary: You will be able to solve large linear systems iteratively with Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel and conjugate gradient methods and check convergence.

nodes.name: Least squares
nodes.desc: Normal equations, QR factorisation and fitting data.
nodes.summary: You will be able to fit models to data by least squares using the normal equations or QR factorisation and know which is more stable.
topics: Stability of QR vs normal equations

nodes.name: Eigenvalue methods
nodes.desc: Power iteration, inverse iteration and the QR algorithm.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute eigenvalues numerically with power iteration, inverse iteration and the QR algorithm.

nodes.name: Interpolation
nodes.desc: Lagrange and Newton polynomials and Runge's phenomenon.
nodes.summary: You will be able to construct interpolating polynomials in Lagrange and Newton form and explain Runge's phenomenon.

nodes.name: Splines
nodes.desc: Piecewise polynomial and cubic spline interpolation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to interpolate data with piecewise polynomials and cubic splines and choose appropriate boundary conditions.

nodes.name: Numerical derivatives
nodes.desc: Finite difference formulas and choosing the step size.
nodes.summary: You will be able to approximate derivatives with finite difference formulas and choose a step size that balances truncation and rounding.
topics: Optimal step size with rounding error

nodes.name: Numerical integration
nodes.desc: Trapezoidal, Simpson's and Gaussian quadrature rules.
nodes.summary: You will be able to approximate definite integrals with trapezoidal, Simpson's and Gaussian quadrature and estimate their errors.

nodes.name: Numerics toolkit
nodes.desc: Implement and test solvers, fitting and quadrature, comparing accuracy against known results.
nodes.summary: You will implement and test root finders, linear solvers, fitting and quadrature routines and compare them against known results.

nodes.name: Euler's method
nodes.desc: Explicit and implicit Euler for initial value problems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to solve initial value problems with explicit and implicit Euler methods and analyse their accuracy and stability.

nodes.name: Runge-Kutta
nodes.desc: RK4, adaptive step sizes and error control.
nodes.summary: You will be able to integrate ODEs with RK4 and adaptive Runge-Kutta methods that control error by adjusting the step size.

nodes.name: Stiff equations
nodes.desc: Why some ODEs need implicit methods and stability regions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to recognise stiff ODEs and explain why implicit methods with large stability regions are needed for them.

nodes.name: Finite differences
nodes.desc: Discretising PDEs such as the heat equation on a grid.
nodes.summary: You will be able to discretise PDEs like the heat equation on a grid and choose stable explicit or implicit schemes.
topics: Explicit scheme for the heat equation

nodes.name: Optimisation methods
nodes.desc: Gradient descent, Newton and quasi-Newton methods for minimisation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to minimise functions numerically with gradient descent, Newton's method and quasi-Newton methods like BFGS.

nodes.name: Sparse matrices
nodes.desc: Sparse storage formats and solving large sparse systems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to store large sparse matrices efficiently and solve sparse systems without forming dense matrices.

nodes.name: Monte Carlo methods
nodes.desc: Random sampling for integration and simulation, and variance reduction.
nodes.summary: You will be able to estimate integrals and simulate systems with random sampling and reduce variance to improve accuracy.
topics: Error decreasing as 1 over root n

nodes.name: Physics simulation
nodes.desc: Simulate a physical system such as orbits or heat flow and check energy and error behaviour.
nodes.summary: You will simulate a physical system such as orbits or heat flow and check energy conservation and error behaviour.
